decisions.reason: The defining envelope solution and joint initial trace are sound. The remark reversed the lower-envelope extremal property: for u=0 the minorant -1 is below u_*=0. Corrected it to greatest lower semicontinuous minorant, as the cited envelope lemma proves; Definition unchanged.

Differentiating eta/(T-t) gives eta/(T-t)^2, a lower bound eta/T^2 rather than an upper bound. Corrected the remark. The exact signed residuals, uniform terminal divergence, and nested compact superlevel proof were checked and are sound; Statement unchanged.

The uniform-continuity supplier defines only the epsilon--delta property, so the former attribution of a modulus definition was inaccurate. F3 now explicitly records the given modulus hypothesis and derives uniform continuity. Translating competitors preserves the velocity and gives both real-infimum inequalities; Statement unchanged.

For u=-t and v=s the maximum is at t=s=0, so open-domain jets are unavailable there. The actual Statement claims relative contacts, which freezing variables proves; the title and proof label now say relative contacts and a remark restricts jet use to interior times. Coercive attainment, penalty bounds and monotone M_alpha localisation were checked; Statement unchanged.

F1 omitted the spatial variable from the supplier initial limits. Restored the exact joint limsup/liminf conditions. Fermat identifies complete derivatives at classical contacts, differentiability supplies both jets for the converse, and the joint initial inequalities squeeze the continuous initial extension. The original hypotheses and Statement remain unchanged.

The annulus covers in steps 1.1 and 2.1 are ambient indexed covers. Added the exact intrinsic-to-ambient compactness supplier and its indexed clause in F6; that theorem uses only finite choice in ZF. The uniform strict-gap contradiction, CC extraction only in case (b), dual inequalities and equicontinuous initial trace are sound; Statement unchanged.

Neither former metric definition citation supplies convergence of sequences of functions. F4 now states the exact uniform-on-each-compact quantifiers as a local convention and gives the epsilon/3 continuity argument, used also before the compact strict gap in step 1.1. Removed the unused uniform-continuity dependency; retained intrinsic compactness only for compact sets. All maximizer sets localize uniformly and both initial limits pass; Statement unchanged.

Both witnesses lie outside the Hopf--Lax definition hypotheses. Defined the extended infimum expression explicitly in F2, including its lower bound and extended-real convention. Independent computations give L=(2+|v|)^2/4 and output t with residual 1; for sqrt(1+p^2), L is -sqrt(1-v^2) on |v|<=1 and infinity outside, with output -t. No supplier finiteness theorem is invoked outside its hypotheses.

The Euclidean interface indexes coordinates by k<n, so x_1 is unavailable for n=1. Replaced the witness by epsilon x_0 in both locations; its gradient has norm epsilon in every n>=1, |epsilon x_0|<=|x|, and it touches from below at zero. Opposite unit directions exclude upper contacts and the norm gradient verifies the equation away from zero. No Statement or Definition section changes.

With H=0 and both boundary values zero, u=-1 and v=1 at positive times satisfy the original one-sided semicontinuity and interior equation but violate the equality clause. The reverse comparison requires v upper semicontinuous and u lower semicontinuous on the initial slab. Added precisely these assumptions to the equality clause, retaining the original one-sided result, cone and speed; step 2.1 now checks the exchanged pair. Also cited the actual strictification supplier.

The uniform-continuity definition cannot supply boundedness or relaxed initial traces. F3 now assigns boundedness to the actual hypotheses and joint traces to the discontinuous-solution definition, removing the unused dependency. Extending envelopes by continuous data meets the half-closed-slab comparison assumptions, two comparisons give uniqueness, and constant shifts give sup-norm contraction; Statement unchanged.

The omitted positive-dimension hypothesis admits R^0={0}, whose open unit ball has empty boundary, so 1-|0| cannot be its boundary distance and no unit directions exist. Added n>=1 to Example and Given, matching the sphere supplier, and cited the actual norm-gradient computation. For these dimensions opposite unit directions prove the contact assertions and x/|x| (a fixed unit vector at zero) attains the boundary distance. This item has no Statement or Definition section.

The local-bump supplier guarantees strict increase somewhere in the small ball, not at or throughout a neighbourhood of the failure point. Corrected F2 to that exact conclusion. Step 2.1 already uses only one point of increase: normalize the lower test at W_*, keep the smooth bump below the continuous upper barrier, and contradict pointwise supremum maximality. Envelope admissibility, initial squeeze and comparison are sound; Statement unchanged.

Added the intrinsic compactness theorem to license the ambient indexed ball cover in step 3.1, and the compact maximum and quartic suppliers for the C1-test approximation. Checked the fixed-test argument uses psi+|z-z0|^2, so its actual epsilon times spatial Laplacian still vanishes uniformly; corrected that error bound and the attribution of the assumed second-order inequalities. Compact C1 smoothing, relaxed initial squeeze, comparison and finite-cover uniform convergence remain sound; Statement unchanged.
